hook_text: Three out of every four active volcanoes on Earth sit on one giant ring. Where is it, and why is it there?
clip_script: Draw a horseshoe around the Pacific Ocean: New Zealand, Indonesia, Japan, Alaska, then all the way down the Americas to Chile. That's the Ring of Fire, forty thousand kilometres of volcanoes. Why there? Because all around the Pacific, ocean plates are diving under other plates. As a plate sinks, it carries water down into the scorching mantle, and that water makes the rock melt, like salt melting ice. The melted rock, magma, rises and bursts through. And if that magma is sticky, it traps gas like a shaken cooldrink, until boom. That is how Vesuvius buried Pompeii and how Mount St Helens blew its side off. South Africa? We sit in the quiet middle of a plate. No active volcanoes here.
visual_style: A whiteboard world map with a glowing horseshoe of dots around the Pacific; a cross-section of one plate diving under another with water droplets and rising magma; a cooldrink bottle shaken and popping into a volcano.
pacing: Map hook, a quick cross-section, a big boom finish.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find out why volcanoes erupt.
